title: Lease Term Agreement Holdings on a Lease — Open and Pending Terms
content:
A lease carries a chain of Lease Term Agreements, and at any moment a leaseholder holds at most one term that is current or on notice (notice given) and at most one pending term that will follow it.

## Governing clause

1. **A new term may be written only when the lease has no other term in pending status.** The check is made on the lease's own term records before the new term is written, and it is the system record of the lease's terms — not anything the resident says — that decides it.
2. Terms that are superseded, completed, terminated early, transferred or cancelled stay on file as history and do not count toward either limit.
3. Because a resident holds only one open lease, the per-customer cap equals that pair: at most **2** open Lease Term Agreements per customer — one current or on notice, and one pending.

## Status reference

| Status of a term on the lease | Counts toward the limits | Blocks writing a new term |
|---|---|---|
| Pending | Yes (the one pending term) | Yes |
| Current | Yes (the one current or on-notice term) | No |
| Notice given | Yes (the one current or on-notice term) | No |
| Superseded, completed, terminated early, transferred, cancelled | No — history only | No |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A lease shows one current term and no pending term: a new term may be written; afterwards the lease holds one current and one pending term, which is the cap of 2.
- A lease shows a current term and a signed renewal that has not started (pending): no further term may be written on that lease while the renewal stays pending.
- A lease shows one current term and three older terms that were superseded: the superseded terms are history and do not count; a new term may be written.
